title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 76-78). X is a space stratified by closed subsets X_i indexed by a poset I, with X_j ⊂ X_i for j<i. The open strata are X_i^* = X_i \ ∪_{j<i} X_j. V_i (calligraphic in the manuscript) is the pro-tubular neighbourhood of X_i^* in X, a 'procespace', i.e. a pro-object of open neighbourhoods. By (51), X_i^* → V_i is a homotopy equivalence of pro-spaces. For a flag (chain) i_0<...<i_n in I, V_{i_0...i_n} = V_{i_0}∩...∩V_{i_n}. This intersection is empty for non-chains.

Top of this page. The assignment flag ↦ V_flag is an inductive system indexed by the opposite of the poset of flags of I under inclusion. Larger flags give smaller intersections, which include into those of subflags. Its values lie in pro-open subsets of X, a category of 'spaces ≈ X'. Together with (53), X is the colimit (gluing) of this diagram. In modern terms this is a diagram over the barycentric subdivision sd(I), the nondegenerate simplices of the nerve of I.

(55)-(57): relative version. Let Z ⊂ X be locally closed (Grothendieck corrects 'fermée' to 'loc^t'). For i with X_i^* ⊂ Z, set V_i^Z = V_i ∩ Z. Since neighbourhoods in Z are traces of neighbourhoods in X, this is the pro-tubular neighbourhood of X_i^* in Z. The claim is that X_i^* ↪ V_i^Z ↪ V_i are homotopy equivalences. More generally, when the relevant strata lie in Z, V^Z_{i_0...i_n} = V_{i_0...i_n}∩Z = ∩_k V^Z_{i_k}. This is the same construction performed intrinsically for the induced stratification Z_i = X_i∩Z of Z. The claim is that V^Z_{flag} → V_{flag} is a homotopy equivalence.

End of page: for J ⊂ I he sets X_J^* = ∪_{i∈J} X_i^* and X_J = ∪_{i∈J} X_i. This prepares the next page. There, for J an 'idéal' (down-closed) X_J^* is closed. For J a 'tranche' (convex) X_J^* is locally closed. Taking Z = X_J^* then gives X_J^* ≃ colim over Drap(J) of V^J_flag.

Purpose: build a combinatorial/homotopical model of a stratified space as a diagram of 'homotopy link' pro-spaces over the flags of the stratification poset. The model should be stable under passing to unions of strata indexed by convex subposets. This is the 'déploiement' of stratified spaces of the title.
errors: (56)/(57) are not true for an arbitrary locally closed Z. Intersecting a tubular neighbourhood with Z need not be homotopy equivalent to the stratum or to the original neighbourhood. One needs Z to be a union of strata, as in the application Z = X_J^* with J a tranche on the next page, and the conical/tubular structure to restrict to Z. Grothendieck does not state this hypothesis here.

The condition 'si X_{i_n} ⊂ Z' is oddly phrased. Since X_{i_k} ⊂ X_{i_n}, it forces the closed strata X_{i_0},...,X_{i_n} into Z. The natural condition is X_{i_k}^* ⊂ Z for all k. As written, the condition is stronger than needed for locally closed Z.

In (56) the composite V_i^Z → V_i being an equivalence is stated alongside X_i^* → V_i^Z. This is fine given (51) and 2-out-of-3, but only once V_i^Z is known to be a genuine pro-tubular neighbourhood in Z, which again needs Z to be a union of strata.

ideas.what: Diagram of intersections of pro-tubular neighbourhoods indexed by the opposite poset of flags (chains) of the stratification poset, with X as its colimit.
ideas.modern_name: Diagram of homotopy links over sd(P) (barycentric subdivision); décollement/exit-path model of a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); Lurie (Higher Algebra App. A, exit paths); Douteau, Haine, Douteau–Waas (holink diagrams over sd(P), 2018-2021)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches a 'dévissage' of stratified structures via tubular neighbourhoods; no explicit flag-indexed diagram there to my knowledge

ideas.what: Pro-tubular neighbourhoods as pro-objects ('procespaces'), avoiding choices of actual tubular neighbourhoods.
ideas.modern_name: Pro-homotopy type of the deleted neighbourhood / germ of neighbourhoods; holink as homotopy-invariant replacement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn; also shape theory (Borsuk, Mardešić–Segal); Edwards–Hastings pro-homotopy

ideas.what: Restriction of the tubular-neighbourhood system to a locally closed union of strata Z, with V^Z = V∩Z homotopy equivalent to V.
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of a stratified space to a convex subposet (sub-stratified space); invariance of homotopy links under restriction
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in Quinn / Hughes / Douteau–Waas frameworks

ideas.what: Unions of strata X_J^* for J ⊂ I; ideals give closed sets, tranches (convex subsets) give locally closed sets.
ideas.modern_name: Closed/locally closed unions of strata for down-closed/convex subposets

missed.claim: Around 1981-82 Grothendieck models a stratified space as the colimit of a diagram of pro-tubular-neighbourhood intersections indexed by the opposite poset of flags of I. This is essentially the 'homotopy link diagram over sd(P)' that later became central in stratified homotopy theory (Douteau, Haine, Douteau–Waas). That literature does not cite these notes.
missed.quote: c'est un système inductif ... par l'ensemble ordonné opposé de celui des drapeaux de I (vu l'inclusion)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Priority/historical interest: it shows Grothendieck's 'déploiement' programme anticipated the flag-indexed link-diagram description of stratified homotopy types. The procespace (pro-object) formulation is an alternative to the holink approach that might handle non-homotopically-stratified (e.g. non-tame) cases.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is mostly a routine relative version (restriction to locally closed unions of strata). The underlying flag-indexed diagram of pro-tubular neighbourhoods is a mild unpublished anticipation of later stratified-homotopy models, but its substance is now known.
transcription_corrections: Neighbourhoods are written in calligraphic script (𝒱_i, 𝒱^Z_i), as on the previous page, not plain V.
The crossed-out condition after 'pour un i tel que' looks like '[-X_i ⊂ Z-]' (the final letter is a struck-over Z/X), not 'X_i ⊂ X'.
First line: 'd'ensembles pro-[?]' is plausibly 'd'ensembles pro-ouverts' (pro-open sets), consistent with procespaces; uncertain.
'dans la Cat des espaces ≈ X' is uncertain; the symbol may be '⊂ X' or '/X'.
(55) margin note reads 'pro-voisinage tubulaire de X_i^* dans Z' (with 'pro').
